description: We are a team of four: Sarah Atif, Nisreen Sherawala, Ibrahim Qaiser, and Matthew Salas. We share an interest in space exploration, technology, innovation, and problem-solving. Together, we bring creativity, teamwork, communication, and research skills, aiming to design an exciting and innovative space mission game.
summary: Mission Architect is an interactive space mission design game that allows players to experience the challenges of planning and carrying out a space mission. Players choose a destination, design and build their spacecraft, and make important decisions throughout the mission to ensure its success. The game combines space exploration, strategic thinking, problem-solving, and teamwork in an engaging, browser-based experience. It aims to make space science more accessible and enjoyable while helping players understand the complexity of spacecraft design, mission planning, and exploration. By turning these concepts into an interactive simulation, Mission Architect encourages creativity, critical thinking, and a deeper interest in space exploration.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Mission Architect lets players experience a full space mission lifecycle: choose a destination, design a spacecraft, launch it, fly it and get a scored debrief.

HOW IT WORKS

  1. Crew: 1–4 players split four roles. Director (budget and testing), Engineer (structure, power, battery, shielding, fuel), Scientist (instruments) and Flight Ops (rocket, orbit, antenna, ground stations). Each role must report "GO" before launch, like a real launch poll.
  2. Mission: six destinations of rising difficulty, each with realistic constraints. Mars gets 43% of Earth's sunlight, Jupiter about 1/27, so players must choose between huge solar arrays and nuclear power. Europa needs heavy radiation shielding. Far targets need stronger comms to send data home.
  3. Build: live gauges show budget, mass vs. rocket capacity, power, data downlink, fuel and lifetime. A 3D model of the spacecraft updates as parts are added, and a science forecast shows how well the design meets the mission goal.
  4. Flight: an animated 3D launch with booster separation, fairing separation, solar array deployment, a transfer orbit and orbit insertion. Random events (solar storms, debris strikes, computer glitches, budget cuts) go to the matching crew role to decide. Testing level affects the chance of part failures.
  5. Debrief: a score out of 1000 across mission success, science return, efficiency and decisions, with plain-language feedback explaining what went wrong and how to fix it.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

Students rarely get to experiment with a whole mission. Mission Architect makes engineering trade-offs visible and memorable: failing, seeing why, and flying again is the core learning loop. Team roles build collaboration and communication. It runs free in any browser on phones, tablets and laptops, so any classroom can use it.

CREATIVITY

A GO/NO-GO launch poll, a flight director voice, mission twists (random constraints like budget cuts or a grounded rocket), agency ranks, a Hall of Fame leaderboard, collectible badges and a mission patch keep it replay-able.

TOOLS

HTML, CSS and JavaScript in a single web page. Three.js for 3D graphics, with procedurally generated planet textures. Web Audio API for the rocket engine sound, music and effects. Kokoro text-to-speech for the flight director voice. Lucide icons and Google Fonts. Built with help from Claude (Anthropic).
